feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 2 (10 cm span, wheel_track 0.12) reduced oval line losses to 0.05 per run, but slalom stayed at 1.0 and s-bend at 0.9, with max_error still about 0.061 to 0.064 m. Span from 6 to 10 cm is therefore not the full fix on tight bends, so the drivetrain is the next variable. Oscillation rose to 0.23 to 0.27 on oval and s-bend, above the 0.08 to 0.16 range of iterations 0 and 1. If the next race shows slalom and s-bend line losses below 1.0 per run with max_error below 0.06 m and oscillation at or below about 0.3, keep wheel_track 0.10 m and keep the span. If losses stay at about 0.9 to 1.0 per run with max_error near 0.06 m, the response is still too slow, so narrow wheel_track further. If oscillation rises above 0.3 while losses persist, the turn is overcorrecting, so keep wheel_track 0.10 m and move the sensor footprint rather than the drivetrain.
requested_changes: Keep the 10 cm span and set wheel_track to 0.10 m (iteration 2 showed slalom and s-bend losses stayed at 0.9 to 1.0 per run at 0.12 m). If losses fall below 1.0 per run, keep it; if they stay at about 1.0 with max_error near 0.06 m, try wheel_track 0.09 m next.

If steering_oscillation rises above 0.3 with losses still present (iteration 2 gave 0.23 to 0.27), test sensor_size 0.016 m, since iteration 2's oscillation range suggests jitter as tape crosses the footprints, and report whether rms_error and oscillation both improve.

If line losses still occur at the same bend after the drivetrain change, test moving the sensors forward from y 0.04 m to y 0.06 m (within the allowed range), so the robot reacts earlier. This is a hypothesis not yet tested in any iteration, so report the step and bend of the first loss to confirm it.
